contract: align(sequences) -> list of aligned rows, one per input sequence, all of the same length, each row equal to its input sequence with '-' gap characters inserted (upper-case amino acids). sequences is a list of 4 to 10 unaligned protein sequences of a BAliBASE reference-1 test case. align is called once per test case in a sandboxed subprocess with a 240 s CPU budget for all 26 cases. Score (maximize): mean sum-of-pairs score over the cases, i.e. the fraction of residue pairs that the structure-based reference alignment places in the same core-block column and the candidate also aligns; the total-column score is reported alongside
notes: Reference alignments and core-block annotations come from the BAliBASE 3.0 archive (reference set 1: RV11 very divergent, RV12 medium divergence); 26 cases with at most 10 sequences and at most 300 reference columns are used so that a CPU-only aligner finishes inside the budget. The SP and TC scores are an independent implementation of the definitions of Thompson et al. (1999) restricted to core blocks, not a port of the bundled bali_score program, and the reference alignments score exactly 1.0 under it (checked in the tests). Scores on this subset are not comparable with published whole-benchmark averages.
protocol_description: Locally implemented evaluator with recorded reference checks; consult the task-specific tests and evidence for their exact scope. This label alone does not establish reproduction of the paper's full experiment.
name: Biology: protein multiple-alignment accuracy on BAliBASE reference alignments
description: Align the unaligned protein sequences of 26 BAliBASE reference-1 test cases, spanning very divergent and medium-divergence families. The evaluator checks that each alignment is a valid gapped version of the input sequences and scores the sum-of-pairs agreement with the structure-based reference alignment on its annotated core blocks.
benchmark: Biology: protein multiple-alignment accuracy on BAliBASE reference alignments
paper_metric: Local protocol; see candidate contract and source adaptation notes

sources.locator: Thompson, Plewniak and Poch (1999): comparison of multiple alignment programs on reference alignments; defines the sum-of-pairs and total-column scores on core blocks implemented here.
Thompson, Koehl, Ripp and Poch (2005): BAliBASE 3.0, the structure-based reference alignments and core-block annotations used as ground truth.
Katoh et al. (2002), MAFFT: an alignment method whose main goal is accurate and fast multiple sequence alignment, the problem this task scores.
BAliBASE download page; the archive BAliBASE_R1-5.tar.gz (reference sets RV11 and RV12 of this task) states no licence and is downloaded by the prepare script rather than redistributed.

limitations: Only 26 of the 82 reference-1 cases are used (at most 10 sequences and 300 reference columns each) so that a CPU-only aligner finishes within the budget; averages are therefore not comparable with published whole-benchmark numbers.

SP and TC are an independent implementation of the published definitions restricted to core blocks; it scores the reference alignments at exactly 1.0 but is not byte-compatible with the bundled bali_score program.
Reference alignments are themselves structure-based estimates of homology, and core blocks cover only part of each alignment.
The references are public, so search feedback can overfit this fixed subset; a candidate aligner should be checked on held-out families before any claim of improved accuracy.

state_of_the_art.statement: No published value for this 26-case subset and local scorer. For context, the progressive-alignment seed reaches mean SP 0.640 (0.400 on the very divergent RV11 cases, 0.816 on RV12) and mean TC 0.480; published aligners report substantially higher SP on the full reference-1 sets, so there is room to improve.

science_relevance.scientific_problem: Align homologous protein sequences so that structurally equivalent residues occupy the same column, especially for families below 20 % identity.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Multiple sequence alignment underlies homology modelling, phylogenetics and functional-site prediction; alignment accuracy on structure-based reference alignments is the standard way the field measures progress, and divergent families remain unsolved.

papers.task_relation: The task scores candidate aligners with the same SP and TC definitions on BAliBASE reference-1 cases.
